Definition: from G4862 and G1525; to enter in company with:--go in with, go with into.
BiblicalUsage: The disciple known to the high priest goes in with Jesus into the palace, and the crowds note that Jesus went not with His disciples into the boat. Going in with someone is sharing their lot, whether it is a palace full of enemies or a boat going on without Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe going in with Jesus is the disciple's calling, even into the palace of the high priest, and I hold that no place is too dangerous to follow Him into.
